intent: Add a controlled, reproducible token-efficiency benchmark under benchmarks/token-efficiency/ that measures whether AMOS's curated MCP verb surface (money_flow, finance_leaks, list_records, get_catalog, search_documents) lets Claude accomplish a business task in fewer total tokens than a generic raw-access agent (list_tables/describe_table/run_sql over the same data). This is evidence for a marketing/investor claim, so the methodology is built to survive a skeptical read: ONE model held constant (anthropic.claude-opus-4-8 on AWS Bedrock via the official Anthropic SDK), both arms reading the SAME Northwind demo dataset (ported verbatim from amos-platform demo_seed.rs + starters.rs), exact per-response token usage summed across the entire tool-use loop, N>=3 runs with reported spread, and an explicit objective equivalent-quality bar per task so a cheap-but-wrong answer scores no win. Pure Python; touches nothing in the Rust workspace and is not a cargo member.

validation_plan.command: python -m py_compile dataset.py tasks.py runner.py benchmark.py arms/*.py
validation_plan.reason: All benchmark modules must compile cleanly under the Python interpreter.

The shared dataset must materialise the expected Northwind fixtures (5 finance customers, 12 invoices, 7 payments, 6 stripe charges, 12 CRM customers, 8 deals, 3 docs) so both arms read identical data.

validation_plan.command: python -c 'validate amos_verbs analysis engine vs demo_seed.rs ground truth'
validation_plan.reason: money_flow/finance_leaks must reproduce the ground truth the platform's demo_seed.rs tests assert (Stripe net $14,400 after excluding the $18k reconciled charge; 90+ receivables $21k = Initech $12k + Hooli $9k; collection cycle 30d-now vs 7d-prior worsening) so Arm A's curated verbs are faithful, not fabricated.

Run the full N=3 sweep over both arms and all 4 tasks against live Bedrock, reading exact per-response token usage and grading every answer against its equivalent-quality bar; produces results/results.json.
The benchmark is pure Python under benchmarks/ and is NOT a workspace member; confirm the Rust workspace build is unaffected.

execution_evidence.output_ref: money_flow: stripe net $14,400 USD (5 charges), $18,000 reconciled+excluded; invoiced $99,000, collected $54,000 (54.5% conversion); cycle 30d vs 7d prior = worsening; Globex top at 54.5% of the in-window base; 90+ = $21,000 (2 invoices). finance_leaks: customer_concentration ($54k), aged_receivables_90 ($21k), aged_receivables_31_90 ($15k) — all match the demo_seed.rs test assertions. (Note: 54.5% is Globex's share of the 90-day-window invoiced base; the seed comment's '~45%' is over a wider base — the quality bar keys on 'Globex' + the aged receivables, robust to either.)

24 trials (2 arms x 4 tasks x 3 runs) against anthropic.claude-opus-4-8 on Bedrock. Per-task raw/amos token ratios: cashflow 5.4x (amos 3,618 / raw 19,613; both 3/3 pass), leaks 5.4x (3,042 / 16,277; 3/3), stale_deals 1.8x (4,921 / 8,856; amos 3/3, raw 1/3 pass — raw dropped a stale deal on 2 runs, an honest QUALITY loss the grader caught), retrieval 2.0x (3,831 / 7,727; 3/3). Overall equal-weight ratio 3.4x. Results in results/results.json.

result_summary: Added a defensible token-efficiency benchmark (benchmarks/token-efficiency/): two arms (curated AMOS verbs vs generic raw-SQL access) over one shared, deterministic Northwind dataset ported from the platform demo seed, one model held constant (anthropic.claude-opus-4-8 on Bedrock), exact per-loop token accounting, N=3 runs, and objective per-task equivalent-quality bars. Result: raw-access costs 5.4x more tokens on curated-analysis tasks (cashflow, leaks), ~2x on CRM/retrieval tasks (stale_deals, retrieval), 3.4x overall equal-weight. On stale_deals the raw agent also failed the quality bar 2/3 runs (misclassified a stale deal), a reliability loss beyond tokens. README documents methodology, quality bars, reproduction, and an explicit honest-findings section (win is task-dependent; this is a faithful model of the surface not the live MCP server; small demo dataset likely understates the production advantage). Pure Python, no Rust workspace impact.
